rationales.whyCorrect: Mucosal, digestive, or transport problems reduce nutrient absorption.
rationales.eli10: Food arrives, but nutrients do not cross into the body well.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Why does untreated type 1 diabetes cause hyperglycemia?

options.text: Insulin deficiency limits uptake and increases hepatic glucose output

rationales.whyCorrect: Without insulin, glucose remains in blood while the liver continues releasing more.
rationales.eli10: The key is missing, so sugar stays outside cells and piles up.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Sweating, tremor, and confusion occur with low glucose. What drives early signs?

options.text: Adrenergic response and brain fuel shortage

rationales.whyCorrect: Counterregulatory activation causes autonomic symptoms, while neuroglycopenia impairs cognition.
rationales.eli10: The alarm makes the body shaky while the brain runs low on fuel.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Why does severe hyperglycemia cause frequent urination?

options.text: Filtered glucose pulls water into urine

rationales.whyCorrect: Glucose exceeding reabsorptive capacity produces osmotic diuresis.
rationales.eli10: Sugar in urine drags extra water out with it.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Why can hypothyroidism cause fatigue and cold intolerance?

rationales.whyCorrect: Reduced thyroid hormone lowers heat production and energy turnover.
rationales.eli10: The body's speed and heater settings are too low.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: A peptic ulcer follows chronic NSAID use. What defense was reduced?

rationales.whyCorrect: NSAIDs reduce prostaglandins that support mucus, bicarbonate, and blood flow.
rationales.eli10: The medicine weakens the stomach's protective coating system.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Why does cirrhosis cause portal hypertension?

options.text: Scarred liver resists portal blood flow

rationales.whyCorrect: Fibrosis and nodules obstruct blood passing through hepatic sinusoids.
rationales.eli10: Blood meets a stiff maze inside the scarred liver.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Why can cirrhosis cause ascites?

options.text: Portal pressure, low albumin, and retention favor fluid accumulation

rationales.whyCorrect: Multiple hemodynamic and hormonal changes shift fluid into the abdomen.
rationales.eli10: High pressure, weak protein pull, and saved salt make a belly puddle.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Pancreatic inflammation causes fat malabsorption by reducing what?

rationales.whyCorrect: Pancreatic lipase is needed to digest triglycerides for absorption.
rationales.eli10: Without fat-cutting scissors, large fat molecules cannot be absorbed well.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Why can small-intestinal villous damage cause multiple deficiencies?

rationales.whyCorrect: Flattened villi provide less membrane for nutrient transfer.
rationales.eli10: Flattening the tiny folds shrinks the gut's catching area.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Which pattern is more typical of Crohn disease than ulcerative colitis?

options.text: Transmural skip lesions anywhere in the GI tract

rationales.whyCorrect: Crohn disease produces patchy full-thickness inflammation from mouth to anus.
rationales.eli10: Deep sore patches can appear with healthy spaces between them.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Why can ulcerative colitis cause bloody diarrhea?

rationales.whyCorrect: Continuous mucosal inflammation creates friable bleeding surfaces.
rationales.eli10: The sore inner colon lining leaks blood into stool.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Type 2 diabetes initially produces high insulin levels. Why?

options.text: Beta cells compensate for tissue resistance

rationales.whyCorrect: The pancreas secretes more insulin to overcome reduced target-cell response.
rationales.eli10: The key factory makes extra keys because the locks are stubborn.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: A person with hyperthyroidism loses weight despite appetite. Why?

options.text: Metabolic rate and energy use rise

rationales.whyCorrect: Excess thyroid hormone increases heat production and substrate turnover.
rationales.eli10: The body burns fuel faster than meals replace it.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Why can chronic malabsorption produce anemia?

options.text: Iron, folate, or B12 uptake may be inadequate

rationales.whyCorrect: Different absorptive defects limit nutrients required for erythropoiesis.
rationales.eli10: The body lacks important building pieces for red cells.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Why can pancreatitis cause low calcium in severe cases?

options.text: Fat necrosis can bind calcium salts

rationales.whyCorrect: Released fatty acids combine with calcium during saponification.
rationales.eli10: Damaged fat traps calcium like soap forming around it.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: How does insulin resistance worsen through elevated free fatty acids?

options.text: Lipids disrupt insulin signaling and promote hepatic glucose output

rationales.whyCorrect: Ectopic lipid and inflammatory signaling reinforce metabolic dysfunction.
rationales.eli10: Extra fat messages jam the insulin signal and tell the liver to release sugar.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Why can liver failure cause confusion?

options.text: Impaired detoxification allows neuroactive substances such as ammonia to accumulate

rationales.whyCorrect: Hepatic encephalopathy reflects toxins, inflammation, and altered neurotransmission.
rationales.eli10: A failing filter lets brain-confusing waste build up.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: A person has high TSH and low thyroid hormone. Where is the primary defect?

rationales.whyCorrect: Low output removes negative feedback, so the pituitary raises TSH.
rationales.eli10: The manager shouts louder because the thyroid factory is underproducing.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Why can diabetic ketoacidosis produce metabolic acidosis?

options.text: Insulin deficiency drives fat breakdown and ketone production

rationales.whyCorrect: Ketone acids accumulate when cells shift toward uncontrolled fatty-acid oxidation.
rationales.eli10: Without insulin, the body burns fat fast and acidic leftovers pile up.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: How does portal hypertension contribute to varices?

options.text: Collateral veins enlarge to bypass the high-resistance liver

rationales.whyCorrect: Blood reroutes through fragile systemic veins that can dilate and rupture.
rationales.eli10: Traffic takes weak side roads when the liver highway is blocked.

subjectWideQuestions.stem: Why can terminal-ileum disease cause both B12 deficiency and bile-salt-related diarrhea?

options.text: The ileum normally absorbs B12 complexes and recycles bile salts

rationales.whyCorrect: Ileal dysfunction prevents two distinct absorption pathways, affecting blood formation and fat handling.
rationales.eli10: One damaged section fails to catch a vitamin package and recycle digestive soap.
